verdict.rationale: Gmail's own filters can match incoming mail by criteria such as sender or subject and automatically apply labels, which lets a user route mail into separate labeled streams. One user reports filtering mis-addressed mail into its own folder this way. However, the pack never documents a split inbox view, priority or important classification, or automatic newsletter and calendar-invite streams; the streams have to be built by hand from filter rules. missing for 10: documented split or multiple-inbox view, automatic important/priority classification, built-in category streams (newsletters, calendar invites, team), priority-order triage workflow, independent corroboration of stream-based triage.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can split my inbox into focused streams — important, team, newsletters, calendar invites — so triage happens in priority order, not arrival order

citations.quote: When a message matches, filters automatically trigger actions such as adding or removing labels, or forwarding the email to a specified address.
Advanced rules configured for an account that evaluate incoming messages against specific matching criteria (like sender, subject, or size).
